lessons.title: ICT, Computer, Data and Information
lessons.notes_html:
ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology. It is a connected system of interactive tools and technologies used to send and receive information, with a focus on communication technology.

The Computer

A computer is an electronic machine that can accept data (input), manipulate the data according to specified rules (process), produce results (output) and store the results for future use.

Data and Information

DataInformation
A collection of raw facts and figures. It is unorganized and not useful by itself. It can be words, numbers, images and sounds.Organized, useful data. It is how you understand the facts, and it is the result of data processing.

So, processed data is called information, and a set of instructions that tells the computer what to do is called a program.

Key Points

  • ICT means Information and Communication Technology.
  • A computer works in four steps: input, process, output and store.
  • Data is raw and unorganized; information is organized and useful.

lessons.title: Input Devices
lessons.notes_html:
An input device allows a user to enter data and commands into the memory of a computer.

Common Input Devices

  • Keyboard — used to type text and commands. The standard keyboard is also called the QWERTY keyboard.
  • Mouse — an input device that looks like a mouse. It has two buttons, left click and right click. Right click displays a pop-up menu with various options.
  • Microphone — used to record audio and voice calls.
  • Digital camera — takes pictures and sends them into the computer.
  • Scanner — scans documents such as photographs, pages of text and books, and converts them into digital format.
  • Biometric sensor — identifies the unique physical characteristics of a person, for example by face, palm, fingerprint or retina and iris scan.

Scanner and Biometric Sensor

A scanner works on documents and books. A biometric sensor works on the body of a person, such as a fingerprint or a face.

Key Points

  • Input devices enter data and commands into the computer.
  • The printer is NOT an input device.
  • A biometric sensor identifies a person by unique physical characteristics.

lessons.title: Output Devices
lessons.notes_html:
An output device is used to show the information generated by a computer to the user.

Common Output Devices

  • Monitor — shows the output on a screen.
  • Printer — prints electronic data on paper. The printed paper is called hard copy.
  • Speakers — produce sound output.
  • Multimedia projector — shows the computer output on a big screen or wall.

CRT and LCD Monitors

CRTLCD
Cathode Ray Tube. The traditional monitor. It is bigger in size and is usually not available in the market now.Liquid Crystal Display. It is smaller, consumes less power, and is more expensive than CRT.

Key Points

  • Output devices show information to the user.
  • Printed paper is called hard copy.
  • LCD is smaller than CRT and consumes less power.

lessons.title: Hardware, Software and Memory
lessons.notes_html:
Hardware means the physical parts of the computer system that can be seen and touched. Software is a set of instructions (a program) that tells the hardware how to do a job. Hardware cannot perform any task without software, and software cannot be executed without hardware.

RAM and ROM

RAMROM
Random Access Memory. Volatile and temporary: contents are lost when the computer is switched off. Reading and writing are both possible. It is fast.Read Only Memory. Non-volatile and permanent: contents are retained even when the device is powered off. The user can only read it. It is slower and cheaper than RAM.

Storage and Other Parts

  • Motherboard — the main circuit board inside the system unit.
  • USB — Universal Serial Bus, used to connect devices.
  • SSD — Solid State Drive, a secondary storage device that accesses data faster than an HDD and keeps data even without power.

Key Points

  • Hardware can be seen and touched; software is a set of instructions.
  • RAM is temporary and volatile; ROM is permanent and non-volatile.
  • An SSD is faster than an HDD.

lessons.title: Generations of Computers
lessons.notes_html:
Computer development is classified into five generations. In every generation, computers became smaller, faster and more reliable.

GenerationPeriodMain technology
First1940 to 1956Vacuum tubes for circuitry and magnetic drum for memory. UNIVAC and ENIAC are examples.
Second1956 to 1963Transistors replaced vacuum tubes. These computers generated less heat.
Third1964 to 1971Integrated circuits (IC) and semi-conductors were used for the first time. Smaller and more reliable.
Fourth1971 to 1985The microprocessor was used, with thousands of integrated circuits on one chip.
Fifth1985 to present and futureBelongs to Artificial Intelligence, with new technologies like speech recognition.

Key Points

  • First generation used vacuum tubes; second used transistors.
  • Integrated circuits were first used in the third generation.
  • The fifth generation is the age of Artificial Intelligence.

lessons.title: The Keyboard and the Modem
lessons.notes_html:
The standard keyboard is called the QWERTY keyboard, after the first letters of its top letter row. It has four main segments.

Segments of the Keyboard

  • Function keys — the 12 keys marked F1 to F12 at the top. Every function key has a different meaning in different software, but F1 is used for HELP in almost all software.
  • Typewriter keys — the main block of letter keys.
  • Cursor control keys — the arrow keys that move the cursor.
  • Numeric keypad — the block on the right side for quick number entry. It has digits 0 to 9, plus / * + - . Num Lock and Enter.

The Modem

A modem is a communications device that enables computers to communicate via telephone lines, so users can exchange data and information with another computer.

Key Points

  • F1 to F12 are function keys; F1 gives help in almost all software.
  • The numeric pad is used for quick number entry.
  • A modem connects computers through telephone lines.

lessons.title: What Is an Operating System?
lessons.notes_html:
An operating system (OS) is system software that manages the hardware of the computer. It manages the computer memory and processes, as well as all of its hardware and software, and it allows you to communicate with the computer.

Why a Computer Needs an OS

Without an operating system, a computer cannot do anything: no program can run and no hardware can be used. The OS is the link between the user, the programs and the hardware.

Microsoft Windows

  • Windows is an operating system designed by Microsoft.
  • It allows you to use a computer through a graphical interface.
  • It is the most popular operating system for home computers.
  • The book names Windows 11 as the newest version.

Key Points

  • An operating system is system software that manages hardware, memory and processes.
  • Windows is designed by Microsoft, not by Apple.
  • Without an OS, a computer cannot work at all.

lessons.title: The Windows Desktop
lessons.notes_html:
The Windows Desktop is the main screen of the operating system. On it you have access to tools like the Start Menu, the Taskbar and other icons.

Desktop Icons

Desktop icons are small images that represent programs, files and folders. Their purpose is to give quick access to frequently used programs, files and folders.

This PC and Recycle Bin

  • This PC — the new name of My Computer in Windows 10. It shows different icons like documents, downloads, music, videos, hard drives, CD and USB.
  • Recycle Bin — a special folder where deleted items are temporarily stored. Deleted files are not permanently removed, and files in the Recycle Bin can be restored to their original location.

Key Points

  • The Desktop is the main screen of the operating system.
  • Icons are small images for programs, files and folders.
  • Deleted items go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored.

lessons.title: Taskbar, Start Menu and Notification Area
lessons.notes_html:
The Taskbar is the most important part of the Desktop. By default it sits at the bottom of the screen.

PartWhat it is
Start buttonA small button that displays the Windows logo, always at the left end of the Taskbar. Clicking it opens the Start menu.
Start menuLocated in the lower-left corner of the screen. It contains all your apps, settings and files, and gives fast access to open any application.
Notification AreaThe right end of the Taskbar. It contains icons of battery, Wi-Fi, volume, Clock and Calendar, and the action center, and provides status and notifications.

You can open the Start menu by clicking the Windows icon, pressing the Windows key, or pressing Ctrl + Esc. The Start button works like a table of contents to all applications and folders.

Key Points

  • The Taskbar sits at the bottom and holds the Start Menu, app icons and the Notification Area.
  • The Start menu is in the lower-left corner, not the lower-right.
  • Battery, Wi-Fi, volume and clock icons live in the Notification Area.

lessons.title: Files and Folders
lessons.notes_html:
A file is a collection of data or information stored in a computer. A folder is a container that contains files or other folders, called subfolders, or both.

Why We Need Folders

Folders let us organize our files so they can be stored, found and managed easily, instead of lying mixed together.

Making a File and a Folder

  • To make a file: double-click This PC, click Documents, open your folder, right-click in the empty area, select New, then Text Document, and rename it.
  • To create a folder on the Desktop: right-click on an empty part of the Desktop, select New, then click Folder, and type a name.
  • Shortcut for a new folder in File Explorer: Ctrl + Shift + N.

Key Points

  • A file stores data; a folder is a container for files and subfolders.
  • Folders keep work organized and easy to find.
  • Ctrl + Shift + N creates a new folder.

lessons.title: Working with Files: Copy, Cut, Delete and Drag
lessons.notes_html:
Windows gives simple tools to move, copy and remove files and folders.

CopyCut
Reproduces a file or folder without removing the original. Shortcut: Ctrl + C, then Paste with Ctrl + V.Moves a file or folder: the original is removed from its first location once it is pasted at the new location. Shortcut: Ctrl + X, then Paste with Ctrl + V.

Deleting and Dragging

  • To delete: select the file or folder, right-click and choose Delete, or use the Delete button in the Ribbon. Click Yes in the confirmation window. The item goes to the Recycle Bin.
  • Dragging means moving the mouse while keeping the mouse button pushed down over a file or folder, moving it to a new location, and then lifting the button to drop it there.

Key Points

  • Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + V pastes, Ctrl + X cuts.
  • Copy keeps the original; Cut removes it after pasting.
  • Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin first.

lessons.title: MS Paint: A First Drawing Program
lessons.notes_html:
MS Paint is application software: a simple graphics editing program. Application software is made for a specific task, unlike the operating system which runs the whole computer.

Why Paint Is Good for Beginners

  • It lets beginners create and edit pictures made up of dots on the screen.
  • Its tools are easy: pencil for free-hand drawing, brushes, shapes, fill with color, text and eraser.
  • It opens and saves common picture files such as JPEG, GIF and PNG.

The unit also introduces Paint 3D and Prezi, which are covered in the last lesson of this unit.

Key Points

  • MS Paint is application software for graphics editing.
  • It is simple, so it is good for beginners.
  • Paint works with JPEG, GIF and PNG picture files.

lessons.title: Parts of the Paint Window
lessons.notes_html:
To use Paint well, you must know the parts of its window.

  • Title bar — a horizontal bar at the top of a window. It displays the title of the software and the name of the current document.
  • Quick Access Toolbar — located at the top left of the Paint window, with quick buttons for common tasks.
  • Ribbon — located below the Quick Access Toolbar and the Title Bar. It provides quick access to commonly used tasks.
  • Toolbox — a pane containing icons and buttons that are tools in the program.
  • Drawing area (Canvas) — a rectangular area that supports drawing and opens images in it. Its corner has a handle to change the canvas size.
  • Color Palette — a set of available colors in the software, shown in the Ribbon.
  • Rulers — used to measure the dimensions of the image.

Key Points

  • The Title bar shows the software name and the document name.
  • Drawing is done on the canvas.
  • Rulers measure the dimensions of the image.

lessons.title: Paint Tools: Pencil, Brush, Shapes and Colour
lessons.notes_html:
Paint tools are selected from the Home tab, and then used inside the drawing area.

Pencil ToolBrush Tool
Used for free-hand drawing of an image. Select Pencil, then click and hold in the drawing area and draw.Used to add additional effects to an image with various textures: calligraphy brush, air brush, oil brush, crayon, marker, natural pencil and watercolor brush.

Shapes and Colour

  • The Shapes tool has many shapes for drawing, such as rectangle, ellipse (circle), triangle, polygon, arrows and lines.
  • Foreground color is used for lines, borders of different shapes and text.
  • Background color is used to fill shapes and the background of text or text boxes.
  • To change the color of a shape: select the shape, then use Fill for the inside colour and Outline for the border colour.
  • To write text in a circle: draw a circle with the Shapes tool, select the Text tool, click inside the circle and type in the text box.

Key Points

  • Pencil is for free-hand drawing; Brush adds texture effects.
  • Foreground color makes lines and borders; background color fills shapes.
  • Fill colours the inside of a shape; Outline colours its border.

lessons.title: Saving Work and Useful Shortcuts
lessons.notes_html:
Shortcut keys make work fast. The same shortcuts work in Paint, Word and most other programs.

ShortcutWork
Ctrl + SSave the file or image
Ctrl + CCopy the selected item
Ctrl + VPaste the copied or cut item
Ctrl + XCut the selected item
Ctrl + ASelect the entire document
Ctrl + PPrint
Alt + F4Close the window

Save and Save As

Save stores the file with its existing name and location. Save As opens a dialog box so you can choose a new folder, a new file name, or a new format before saving. To save a document the first time: click File, select Save (or press Ctrl + S), choose the folder, enter the file name and press Save.

Key Points

  • Ctrl + S saves, Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + V pastes, Ctrl + X cuts.
  • Ctrl + A selects the entire document.
  • Save As lets you change the name, folder or format.

lessons.title: MS Word, Prezi and Editing Keys
lessons.notes_html:
Microsoft Word is a word processing application that allows you to create a variety of documents. In a document, text can be lined up with alignment: at the left edge, centered, at the right edge, or spread evenly (justified). Bullets are small symbols, such as dots, placed at the start of each item in a list.

Delete and Backspace

Delete KeyBackspace Key
Deletes text to the RIGHT of the insertion point.Deletes text to the LEFT of the insertion point.

Choosing a Template in Prezi

  • Log in to Prezi and view your dashboard.
  • Select Prezi Presentation on the left side of the screen.
  • Click Create from template, scroll down and select a template according to your requirement.
  • Click Use this Template.

Key Points

  • MS Word is a word processing application.
  • Delete removes text on the right; Backspace removes text on the left.
  • In Prezi, presentations can start from a ready template.

lessons.title: What Is the Internet?
lessons.notes_html:
The Internet, also called the Net, is a global network of billions of computers and other electronic devices. It is the largest network in the world: a network of networks made up of millions of private, public, business and government networks.

History in Short

  • ARPANET stands for Advanced Research Projects Agency Network, an early network.
  • NSF stands for National Science Foundation.
  • Networks are connected by physical cables (copper telephone wires, TV cables and fiber optic cables) and by wireless connections like Wi-Fi and 3G/4G.

Getting Connected: ISP

ISP stands for Internet Service Provider. The type of service you get depends on your ISP: dial-up (slowest, uses a phone line), DSL (broadband, much faster than dial-up), cable (via cable TV), satellite (through satellites) and 3G/4G (wireless, mostly for mobile phones). DSL service uses a broadband connection.

Key Points

  • The Internet is a global network of networks.
  • An ISP provides your internet connection.
  • Dial-up is the slowest type; DSL is broadband.

lessons.title: The Web, Websites and Web Servers
lessons.notes_html:
WWW stands for World Wide Web, or the Web. It is a collection of different websites on the Internet, and it was developed in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee.

Website and Web Server

WebsiteWeb Server
Made up of related text, images and other resources. It has a purpose, such as news, an online library or education. It lives on the Internet.A computer where websites are stored. When you visit a website, your computer sends a request to the server, and the server sends the correct data back.

Remember: the Internet is the network itself, while the Web is the collection of websites that runs on it. A server is a computer where websites are stored; it is not the tool you search with.

Key Points

  • The Web is a collection of websites on the Internet.
  • The WWW was developed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.
  • Websites are stored on web servers.

lessons.title: Browsers, Search Engines and Links
lessons.notes_html:
Two different tools help you use the Web. Do not mix them up.

Web BrowserSearch Engine
Software that finds and displays websites, for example Google Chrome, Safari, Mozilla Firefox, Internet Explorer and Opera. The browser itself is not the Internet.A tool that finds information on the Internet, for example Google, Yahoo! and Bing. You type keywords and it returns a list of relevant websites. Search engines make information easier to find.

URL and Hyperlink

  • URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. Each website has a unique address called a URL. Type it into the browser address bar and press Enter to go directly to the web page.
  • A hyperlink, or link, is a word or phrase on a website that is blue or underlined in blue. Clicking it usually takes you to a different webpage. Your cursor changes into a hand icon when you hover over a link.

Key Points

  • A browser displays websites; a search engine finds information.
  • A URL is the unique address of a website.
  • Links are blue or underlined, and the cursor becomes a hand over them.

lessons.title: Uploading, Downloading and Bookmarks
lessons.notes_html:
Data moves in two directions between your computer and the Internet.

UploadingDownloading
Sending data or a file from your computer to somewhere on the Internet.Receiving data or a file from the Internet onto your computer, for example saving a file by clicking its link.

Saving and Remembering Pages

  • To save an image: right-click the image and select Save image as (or Save picture as).
  • Favorites, also called bookmarks, save a website you want to view later, so you do not have to memorize its exact address. Click the Star icon to bookmark the current website.
  • Your browser also keeps a history of every site you visit.
  • If several tabs are open that you do not want to lose, use bookmarks so you can come back to them later.

Key Points

  • Uploading sends data to the Internet; downloading receives data from it.
  • Bookmarks save pages for later.
  • Right-click an image to save it to your computer.

lessons.title: Searching Well and Checking Information
lessons.notes_html:
A search engine such as Google, Yahoo! or Bing can find almost anything, if you search in the right way.

How to Search

  • Open the search engine, type one or more keywords and press Enter.
  • You will see a list of relevant websites, called search results. Click a link to open a site, or go back to the results for more options.
  • If the first try fails, try different keywords or use the search suggestions.
  • Exclude a word with a minus sign, for example: cake recipe -chocolate.
  • Put an exact phrase in quotation marks to search for those exact words.

Check Before You Believe

Everything on the Internet is not from an authentic source. Consider the source, read to the end, analyze the facts, check other sources, and watch out for errors before you believe any information. Note also that 5G is the fifth generation of mobile network technology.

Key Points

  • Keywords give search results; better keywords give better results.
  • Use a minus sign to exclude a word and quotes for an exact phrase.
  • Always check the source of information.

chapters.title: Unit 5: Algorithmic Thinking and Problem Solving

lessons.title: Problems and Problem Solving
lessons.notes_html:
A problem is a situation or an issue that needs to be solved.

Simple ProblemsComplex Problems
Straightforward and easy to understand, with a clear solution.More challenging, with many parts or steps.

Steps of Problem Solving

  • Identifying the problem — figuring out what the problem is: what is going wrong or what needs to be fixed. Example: you cannot find your favourite book.
  • Gather information about the problem.
  • Think of solutions (brainstorming).
  • Evaluate the solutions and choose the best one.
  • Implement the chosen solution.
  • Check if it worked, and learn from the experience (reflecting).

Key Points

  • A problem is a situation that needs to be solved.
  • Simple problems are easy; complex problems have many parts.
  • Identifying the problem is the first step of problem solving.

lessons.title: What Is an Algorithm?
lessons.notes_html:
An algorithm is a set of clear, step-by-step instructions that help you solve a problem or complete a task. In short, it is a set of rules to be followed. Step-by-step presentation of the solution of a problem is called an algorithm.

Origin of the Word

The word algorithm is derived from the name of the mathematician Mohammed ibn-Musa al-Khwarizmi (born 780 AD in Iraq; died 850 AD).

First and Last Steps

  • The first step of every algorithm is Start.
  • The last step of every algorithm is End.
  • Between Start and End, each step must be written in the right order.

Writing an algorithm means creating a step-by-step procedure or set of rules to solve a specific problem or perform a task, before any coding is done.

Key Points

  • An algorithm is a step-by-step set of rules to solve a problem.
  • Its name comes from the mathematician al-Khwarizmi.
  • Every algorithm begins with Start and finishes with End.

lessons.title: Qualities of a Good Algorithm
lessons.notes_html:
A good algorithm is easy for anyone to follow and gives the correct result every time.

OrderedUnambiguous
The steps are in the right sequence to get the correct result. Example: you must mix the ingredients before baking them.There is no confusion about what each step means. Example: instead of saying only heat, specify heat on medium for 5 minutes.

Well-Defined Steps

  • Every step should be clear and precise, and not confusing.
  • The steps must be in the right order to get the correct result.
  • Steps should be specific and detailed. Instead of just saying make a sandwich, the steps should clearly say what to do, like spread peanut butter.

Key Points

  • Steps must be clear, precise and in the right order.
  • Ordered means correct sequence; unambiguous means no confusion.
  • Vague steps give wrong or different results.

lessons.title: Decisions: IF and GOTO Statements
lessons.notes_html:
Programs often need to make decisions or jump to another step. Two statements do this work.

IF StatementGOTO Statement
Used to make decisions in a program. It does something only if a certain condition is true; if the condition is false, it does nothing. Example: If it is raining, then bring an umbrella.A shortcut that changes where the program is looking next. The computer moves to a different part of the program and starts running instructions from there. Example: in a game, choosing to skip to the next level. It does not test a condition by itself.

The process of writing a program is called programming (coding), and programming is a skill to understand and solve a computational problem.

Key Points

  • IF checks a condition and acts only when it is true.
  • GOTO jumps the program to a different part.
  • Writing a program is called programming.

lessons.title: Writing Algorithms: Worked Examples
lessons.notes_html:
An algorithm is written before coding. A program is the set of instructions written in a specific language that a computer can understand and execute.

Example 1: Greater of Two Numbers

  • Step 1: Start. Step 2: Take two inputs, a and b, from the user.
  • Step 3: If a is greater than b, go to Step 4, otherwise go to Step 5.
  • Step 4: Print a is greater than b, then go to Step 6. Step 5: Print b is greater than a. Step 6: End.

Example 2: Calculate 2(3 + 5)

  • Step 1: Start. Step 2: Follow the order of operations: brackets first, then multiplication.
  • Step 3: Solve inside the brackets: 3 + 5 = 8. Step 4: Multiply: 2 x 8 = 16.
  • Step 5: Print the result, 16. Step 6: End.

Advantages of Algorithms

Algorithms break a problem into manageable steps and solve it efficiently. Writing the algorithm before coding resolves errors and confusions, makes the steps easy to understand and test, and lets anyone follow the same steps to reach the same correct result.

Key Points

  • Decisions inside an algorithm use IF and GOTO steps.
  • Brackets are solved before multiplication.
  • A clear algorithm makes coding easier and safer.

lessons.title: Programs and Programming Languages
lessons.notes_html:
A program is a set of well-defined instructions given to the computer to do a task. Code is a set of logical, mathematical and sequential instructions.

The Compiler

A compiler is a special program that translates code written in a high-level programming language into machine code, which the computer hardware can directly execute. It works in three steps:

  • Source code — the programmer writes code in a high-level language like C++, Java or C#.
  • Compilation — the compiler checks the source code for errors and converts it into machine code or an intermediate code.
  • Output — the result is usually an executable file, like .exe on Windows, that the computer can run.

Key Points

  • A program is a set of instructions for doing a task.
  • A compiler converts a high level language program into machine language.
  • A compiler does NOT convert a middle language program into a high level language.

lessons.title: Low, Middle and High Level Languages
lessons.notes_html:
Programming languages are grouped by how close they are to the computer hardware or to human language.

LevelMeaning
Low level (machine language)The most basic language, directly understood by the computer hardware. It consists of binary code (0s and 1s), for example 10101000, and it is very difficult to learn.
Middle level (assembly language)Uses more symbols and abbreviations in instructions, instead of only 0s and 1s.
High level languagesDesigned to be easy for humans to read and write. They need a compiler to change them into machine language.

Key Points

  • Machine language is binary code: only 0s and 1s.
  • Assembly language uses symbols and abbreviations.
  • High level languages are easy for humans to read and write.

lessons.title: High Level Languages and Their Uses
lessons.notes_html:
Each high level language is popular for a different kind of work.

LanguageUses
PythonArtificial Intelligence, data science, web development, automation and scripting, and social media applications. Instagram uses Django, a Python framework.
JavaScriptWebsites and mobile application development. Gmail and Google Maps use it for smooth user experiences.
JavaInternet programming and Android mobile applications.
C#Mobile devices and video games, for example Angry Birds 2 and Monument Valley.
C / C++Hardware programming such as automobiles and medical devices, for example microcontrollers and embedded systems.

Other high level languages named in the book include Go, R, Swift, PHP and Scratch.

Key Points

  • Python is used in AI and data science.
  • JavaScript is used in websites and mobile apps.
  • Java is used for Android apps; C# is used in games.

lessons.title: Scratch: Programming with Blocks
lessons.notes_html:
Scratch is a visual programming language and online community designed primarily for children and beginners to help them learn the basics of coding. It was developed by the MIT Media Lab (USA) in 2003.

Blocks, Scripts and the Interface

  • Scratch programming deals with creating a script with the help of blocks.
  • Blocks are the units of Scratch programming. Each block has its own functions and properties. Multiple blocks joined together become a program that works as a single unit.
  • A script is the program that tells the actor what to do.
  • The Scratch interface consists of 3 sections.
  • Scratch is used to make stories, animations and games through animations and visual effects — not system software.
  • Some blocks have pull-down menus, for example the play drum block (snare drum, bass drum, side stick, crash cymbal, open hi-hat) and the when key pressed block.

Key Points

  • Scratch was developed by the MIT Media Lab in 2003.
  • In Scratch you join blocks to create a script.
  • Scratch makes stories, animations and games.

lessons.title: Stage, Sprites and Loops in Scratch
lessons.notes_html:
Every Scratch project has actors and a place where they act.

StageSprite
The area where your project comes to life, like a theater stage where all the action takes place. Actors act here and information is displayed here.An object or actor used for developing a program. You can choose one from the library, paint your own, upload an image, or take a picture from a webcam.

Running a Project and Loops

  • Clicking the green flag is a common way to test and run Scratch projects. The when green flag clicked block starts a script; click the red stop button to stop.
  • A loop is a programming structure that repeats a set of instructions or code until a certain condition is met. Again and Again or Repeat represents a loop.
  • Useful blocks: say block shows a message in a bubble, move block moves the sprite some steps, pen down makes the sprite draw a line behind itself, and play drum plays sounds.

Key Points

  • The stage is where the action happens; sprites are the actors.
  • The green flag runs a project; the red button stops it.
  • A loop repeats instructions until a condition is met.

lessons.title: Digital Citizenship and Digital Ethics
lessons.notes_html:
Digital Citizenship refers to the responsible and ethical use of technology by individuals when interacting online. Digital Ethics refers to the principles and moral guidelines that govern the responsible use of technology and the internet.

Key Aspects of Digital Citizenship

  • Online safety — protecting personal information, understanding privacy settings, and being aware of scams, phishing and cyberbullying.
  • Respectful communication with others online.
  • Ethical use of information — citing sources, avoiding plagiarism and respecting copyright.
  • Digital literacy — knowing how to use technology well.
  • Responsible participation in online communities.
  • Balancing technology use — managing screen time and health effects.

Key Points

  • A digital citizen uses technology responsibly and ethically.
  • Protect personal information and learn the privacy settings.
  • Respect others and respect copyright.

lessons.title: Copyright, Plagiarism and Piracy
lessons.notes_html:
Three important words protect the work of creators. Learn the difference between them.

TermMeaning
CopyrightA law that helps protect creative works and ideas. If you create something original, like a drawing, a story or a song, you have the right to decide how others can use it. It gives creators exclusive rights to use and distribute their creations.
PlagiarismUsing someone else's work, ideas or expressions without proper acknowledgment, presenting them as your own.
PiracyThe unauthorized use, distribution or reproduction of copyrighted materials, such as music, movies, software or books, without permission from the copyright holder.

Avoiding Plagiarism

Copying text without credit, paraphrasing ideas without citing the source, and submitting someone else's work as your own are all plagiarism. It can lead to academic penalties, loss of credibility, legal consequences and damage to reputation. Avoid it by giving credit, using your own words, and citing sources. Piracy is illegal and unethical because it deprives creators of revenue and recognition.

Key Points

  • Copyright protects creators and their original work.
  • Plagiarism is passing off another person's work as your own.
  • Piracy is using or sharing copyrighted material without permission.

lessons.title: Staying Safe and Secure Online
lessons.notes_html:
Simple habits keep your computer and your accounts safe.

Safety Rules

  • Antivirus software must be installed in the computer to save it from viruses.
  • Before using a USB drive or external hard drive on your computer, always scan it with antivirus software.
  • Use two-factor authentication (2FA) to add an extra layer of security to your email account.
  • Do not open emails and attachments from a suspicious source.
  • Use strong passwords and keep them private.

Good Computer Habits

  • Use bookmarks for tabs you do not want to lose, so you can come back to them later.
  • Remember: pressing the power button directly to close your computer will likely only put the machine in sleep or hibernation mode. Shut down properly from the menu.

Key Points

  • Scan every USB drive with antivirus before use.
  • Two-factor authentication makes accounts safer.
  • Never open attachments from suspicious sources.

lessons.title: ICT and Health: RSI, Back, Neck and Eyes
lessons.notes_html:
Using ICT devices carelessly can harm health. Each problem has a simple prevention.

ProblemCause and Prevention
RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury)Painful swelling of joints such as shoulder, wrist and fingers, from repeatedly clicking a mouse or typing. Prevention: take breaks to rest your hands, use an ergonomic keyboard and mouse, use a wrist rest pad, and keep enough space to work comfortably.
Back and neck acheCaused by sitting incorrectly (poor posture) or using a chair without back rests. Prevention: take regular breaks to stretch, use adjustable chairs, sit upright against the back rest, and keep feet flat on the floor or use a footrest.
Eye strain and headachesEye strain starts when staring at a computer screen for too long and can blur vision. Prevention: take breaks every hour to rest your eyes, use TFT screens rather than CRT, use an anti-glare screen, ensure good room light, and have your eyes tested regularly.

Key Points

  • RSI harms the shoulder, wrist and fingers; rest your hands often.
  • Sit correctly with back support to protect your back and neck.
  • Rest your eyes every hour to avoid eye strain.

lessons.title: Entrepreneurship and Digital Entrepreneurship
lessons.notes_html:
Entrepreneurship is the process of starting and running a new business or venture.

Digital Entrepreneurship

Digital entrepreneurship is the process of creating and managing a business primarily online, using digital technologies and the internet to deliver products or services. In short, it is the smart application of the power of digital technologies to business.

  • Digital entrepreneurs use websites, social media, e-commerce and mobile apps to reach customers, market their offerings and operate their businesses.
  • Its three principal components are the vision, the technology and the strategy.
  • A manufacturer utilizes raw materials to create products that are then sold in the market.
  • Famous founders: Facebook was created by Mark Zuckerberg, Uber was introduced by Travis Kalanick, Alibaba was founded by Jack Ma, and Jingdong (JD.com) was founded by Richard Liu in 1998.

Key Points

  • Entrepreneurship means starting and running a new business.
  • Digital entrepreneurship runs the business primarily online.
  • Vision, technology and strategy are its three components.

lessons.title: Traditional and Digital Entrepreneurship
lessons.notes_html:
The digital age has changed how businesses work. Compare the two models carefully.

Traditional EntrepreneurshipDigital Entrepreneurship
Relies on physical locations, face-to-face interactions and conventional practices, like retail stores, shops and restaurants.Creates and manages the business primarily online, using websites, social media, e-commerce and mobile apps.
Needs more capital, plus place, furniture, transport, staff and other utilities. Entering the market and distribution are difficult, and work is slower.Cost-effective. Entering the market and distribution are easy, and work is faster. The workplace is digital, not physical.
Works at fixed timings, with less flexible customer service. Communication is face to face. Structure is hierarchical.Works 24/7. Communication is through computers and digital technologies. Structure is flexible and collaborative.
Customers can try a product before buying it. Marketing uses print ads, television, radio and in-person sales, for local markets.Customers cannot try a product before buying; they rely on reviews and specifications. Marketing is digital and worldwide.

Key Points

  • Traditional business needs a physical place; digital business works online 24/7.
  • Digital business is cheaper and faster to start.
  • In digital business, customers cannot try products before buying.

lessons.title: Areas of Digital Entrepreneurship
lessons.notes_html:
Digital entrepreneurship can be applied to many sectors of life.

  • Agriculture — digital platforms connect farmers with buyers; smart farming uses sensors and data analytics; drones monitor crops for precision agriculture.
  • Trading — online trading platforms for buying and selling stocks or commodities, often using algorithms and data analysis.
  • Manufacturing — digital tools for automation, like robotics and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, improve efficiency in production lines; digital twins simulate and optimize processes.
  • Education — online learning platforms such as e-learning courses and educational apps, with virtual classrooms and digital resources.
  • Real Estate — digital platforms list properties, conduct virtual tours and connect buyers with agents; data analytics helps in market analysis and pricing.

Key Points

  • Digital entrepreneurship works in agriculture, trading, manufacturing, education and real estate.
  • Farmers can reach buyers directly through digital platforms.
  • Online learning and virtual tours are digital business in action.

lessons.title: E-Commerce
lessons.notes_html:
E-commerce (electronic commerce) refers to the buying and selling of goods and services over the internet, through digital platforms rather than traditional brick-and-mortar stores.

Key Aspects of E-Commerce

  • Online stores — websites or apps where businesses and individuals list and sell products, for example Amazon, eBay, Alibaba and Shopify stores.
  • Payment systems — credit and debit cards, digital wallets like PayPal and Alipay, and bank transfers, with secure payment gateways.
  • Shopping experience — product searches, reviews, ratings and personalized recommendations. Customers can view products, compare prices and order from anywhere in the world.
  • Order fulfillment — storing, packaging and shipping products, through the business's own logistics or third-party fulfillment centers.
  • Customer service — live chat, email support and help centers.
  • Digital marketing — strategies used to promote products and attract customers online, using social media, phones and other electronic devices.

Key Points

  • E-commerce is buying and selling over the internet.
  • Payments are made by cards, digital wallets and bank transfers.
  • Reviews and ratings help customers choose products.

lessons.title: The Entrepreneurship Process and Amazon's Story
lessons.notes_html:
The entrepreneurship process, how to start a business, has six steps.

Six Steps

  • 1. Idea Generation — come up with a new idea for a product or service that solves a problem, makes life easier, or is just fun. This is the first step.
  • 2. Research — learn more: Will people like this? Is anyone else doing this?
  • 3. Planning — make a plan like a roadmap: how the business will work, what you need, and how much money it will cost.
  • 4. Start the Business — put the plan into action, create the product or service and start selling it.
  • 5. Manage and Grow — keep customers happy, keep track of money, and make the business better.
  • 6. Evaluate and Improve — check how the business is going, fix what is not working, and keep improving.

How Amazon Started

Amazon started as a small online bookstore in 1994. It was created by Jeff Bezos, who began in his garage in Seattle, Washington, to sell books all over the world using the internet. It became popular because buying books online was easy. Then Amazon added music, movies, electronics and toys, and today it is known for fast shipping and a wide selection.

Key Points

  • Idea Generation is the first step of the entrepreneurship process.
  • A plan works like a roadmap for the business.
  • Amazon began in 1994 as an online bookstore in a garage.
